tasks.short: Demonstrate daily living skills step by step, guide students as they practise, make picture step cards and tick off skills mastered.

steps.what: Special education teacher demonstrates daily living skills such as hygiene, safety and food preparation
Special education teacher guides students as they practise in the training kitchen
Special education teacher draws picture step cards for each skill
Special education teacher ticks off skills mastered: on a paper checklist today, on a tablet checklist linked to the plan goals after the change

tasks.design: A library of picture sequences for daily living skills in the learning platform ({LMS}) prints step cards per student, and a tablet checklist linked to the student's plan goals records skills mastered; ticking keeps its time as a first record. Demonstrating and guiding practice stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Step cards were drawn or pasted by hand and checklists kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Picture libraries and tablet checklists linked to plan goals exist for special education.
tasks.still_hard: Each student needs the steps broken down differently.
tasks.human_edge: Staying calm while a student handles a hot pan for the first time.

reach.learn: Whether shared cards make practice consistent across staff.

evidence.claim: Picture sequence libraries and tablet checklists linked to plan goals are available to special education.
Parents' and pupils' councils must consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from skill goals to the skills record; plan reviews are outside.
Input contract: skill goals in the student's plan; picture library kept by the school; fallback is drawing by hand.
Demonstrating and guiding do not change.
Assistants' time is outside the teacher's savings.
Ticking skills mastered is a first record and keeps its full time; only the step cards (s3 at 40) save time.
research_questions: Do students reach skills sooner with consistent cards?

incremental.description: Special education teacher adds new sequences to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library lacks sequences for many of the students' skills, so card making keeps 70 (4.0); high: most cards printed from the library (8.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan test sessions, administer standardized tests with adjustments, score them against norms, interpret the results and put them in the student file.

steps.what: Special education teacher plans test sessions and prepares test materials
Special education teacher administers standardized ability and achievement tests
Special education teacher scores the tests with norm tables: by hand today; after the change the platform scores its tests and paper administrations are still scored by hand
Special education teacher interprets results to determine students' strengths and needs
Special education teacher checks the scores before they go to the student file: right student, test, adjustments noted and norm table
Special education teacher enters results in the student file: typed today; after the change platform scores are released by export and paper scores are still typed

tasks.design: Standardized tests run on the test publisher's platform ({OTHER}), which plans sessions, scores answers against the published norms and exports scores, which the teacher checks and releases once to the student records system. Administering the test with adjustments and interpreting the results stay with the teacher; scoring is fixed norm tables, not AI.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests were scored by hand with norm tables and scores typed into the file.
tasks.enabler_now: Test platforms score against norms and export to records systems.
tasks.still_hard: Paper versions and adjusted administrations still need hand scoring.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a student froze rather than did not know.

reach.learn: Whether shared scores speed up assessments.

evidence.claim: Test platforms score standardized tests against published norms and export results.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets a pupil's level is high-risk; norm tables in code are not AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from the test calendar to results on file; the support plan is outside.
Input contract: norms from the test publisher; fallback is hand scoring.
Administering and interpreting do not change.
Paper administrations are scored and typed by hand; about 70% of tests run on the platform, so s3 and s5 keep 35. The check before the release keeps its full time.

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; checking exported scores is step s5b.

approvals.approved_version: The test scores per student exactly as checked by the teacher in s5b, released once to the student records system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many tests are given on paper or with adjustments the platform does not support, so scoring and typing keep 70 (12.7); high: about 70% on the platform as assumed (22.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare lesson materials and activities, write the lesson plan in the school format, set out materials, keep plans available and discuss preparation with the supervisor.

steps.what: Special education teacher prepares for assigned classes with materials and activities

loop.input: The lesson objective, the level groups and the school's material bank; no student data.
loop.output: Draft activities and worksheets per level group.
loop.check: Code checks each activity is tagged to the lesson objective; the teacher reads every activity against the objective and the level group and rewrites activities that do not fit before use.
loop.stop: Approved by the teacher, or after two redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Activities for mixed levels need free text; the material bank alone does not cover every group.

steps.what: Special education teacher writes the lesson plan in the school format
Special education teacher prints and sets out materials
Special education teacher files lesson plans in a folder as written evidence of preparation
Special education teacher discusses the preparation with the supervisor upon request

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts activities and worksheets per level group from the lesson objective and the school's material bank, and the teacher edits every activity. A lesson plan template in the learning platform ({LMS}) fills objectives, groups and materials, and saved plans are available to the supervisor there instead of in a folder. Setting out materials and talking with the supervisor stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activities and plans were written from scratch and kept in paper folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft activities, and platforms store plans for supervisors.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts rarely fit students with complex needs without heavy editing.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which activity will keep a restless group engaged.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits drafted activities instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether online plans make reviews shorter.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers, ChatGPT plus a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with no quality difference found.
Staff councils must consent to tools that can monitor staff, such as supervisors viewing plans.

assumptions: Boundary: from lesson objectives to the supervisor's discussion; teaching is outside.
Input contract: objectives from the course outline; material bank kept by the department; fallback is writing by hand.
Setting out materials and discussing do not change.
No student data go into the drafting step.
s1 keeps 70 because the teacher edits every drafted activity; s2 keeps 55 because objectives, groups and materials are filled but the lesson's course is still written.
research_questions: How much drafted material is used after editing?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher edits drafted activities.
Special education teacher checks the filled lesson plan.

incremental.description: Special education teacher adds good activities to the material bank.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: students with complex needs require heavier editing, so s1 keeps 85 and s2 keeps 75 (21.2); high: drafts and the template used as designed (32.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up local services, meet parents to guide them, show techniques for dealing with the impairment, put together the list of services discussed and send it to the parents.

steps.what: Special education teacher looks up local services and support for the family
Special education teacher meets with parents to provide guidance in using community resources
Special education teacher teaches parents skills for dealing with students' impairments
Special education teacher puts together the list of services discussed
Special education teacher checks the service list before it goes: the services discussed, current contacts, to the right parents
Special education teacher sends the checked list of services to the parents: by e-mail today, one send through the parent app after the change

tasks.design: The municipality's shared social map ({OTHER}) lists local services and support with contacts, so the teacher picks from it instead of searching. After the meeting the teacher ticks the services discussed, and the teacher checks the list with contacts and sends it once to the parents through the parent app. Guiding parents and teaching skills stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Services were searched for each time and lists written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Municipalities keep social maps of local services.
tasks.still_hard: The social map is not always current.
tasks.human_edge: Helping parents accept support they feared to ask for.

reach.learn: Whether shared lists help families follow up.

evidence.claim: Municipal social maps list local services and support with contacts.
Parents' and pupils' councils must consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from family needs to the list sent; contacting services is outside.
Input contract: social map kept by the municipality; fallback is searching.
Guiding and teaching do not change.
Parents' time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: Do families contact the services listed?

incremental.description: Special education teacher reports outdated entries to the municipality.

approvals.approved_version: The list of services with contacts exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the student's parents through the parent app; changes need a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the social map is incomplete for this family's needs, so look-up keeps 80 (9.0); high: the map covers the services (15.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps teaching skills, testing, interpreting and guiding parents; hand scoring, paper folders and lists written by hand shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved hours on life-skills practice with students.
